2 doubt was entertained as to whether the writ petitions filed invoking Article 226 of the Constitution of India could be transferred to a statutory Tribunal. Hence, the matter is placed before this bench to be decided on the judicial side. 
2. The learned counsel for the petitioner in the writ petitions would fairly concede that transfer of a writ petitions filed under Article 226 to a statutory Tribunal may set a bad precedent. Hence, while concluding that in view of the constitution of the Tribunal, the writ petitioners have to approach the Tribunal, the writ petitions are dismissed with liberty to the petitioners to approach the Tribunal. 
The original orders of the authority, that is impugned in these writ petitions, are directed to be returned to the petitioners and the Tribunal will entertain the appeals without going into the question of limitation if the appeals are filed within a period eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of the original orders of the authority from this Court. There shall be no order as to costs. 
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
